question.text:
A queue is implemented using two stacks $\text{S1}$ and $\text{S2}$.

Use the implementation where $\texttt{dequeue()}$ is $\text{O(1)}$ by keeping the front of the queue at the top of $\textbf{S1}$. Stack $\text{S2}$ is used temporarily during $\texttt{enqueue()}$.

Starting with both stacks empty, perform the following queue operations:

enqueue(1)
enqueue(2)
enqueue(3)
dequeue()
dequeue()
enqueue(4)
enqueue(5)

What are the final contents of $\text{S1}$ and $\text{S2}$?

  1. S1 top to bottom: 3, 4, 5
S2: empty

  2. S1 top to bottom: 5, 4, 3
S2: empty

  3. S1 top to bottom: 3
S2 top to bottom: 5, 4

  4. S1 top to bottom: 4, 5, 3
S2: empty
question.subject: Data Structures

question.text:
Suppose a circular queue of capacity $(n - 1)$ elements is implemented with an array of $n$ elements.

Insertion and deletion operations are carried out using $\texttt{REAR}$ and $\texttt{FRONT}$ as array index variables, respectively.

Initially:

$\texttt{REAR = FRONT = 0}$

Which conditions correctly detect queue full and queue empty?

  1. Full:  (REAR + 1) mod n == FRONT
Empty: REAR == FRONT

  2. Full:  (REAR + 1) mod n == FRONT
Empty: (FRONT + 1) mod n == REAR

  3. Full:  REAR == FRONT
Empty: (REAR + 1) mod n == FRONT

  4. Full:  (FRONT + 1) mod n == REAR
Empty: REAR == FRONT

question.text:
A FIFO queue is represented using a circular linked list and only one external pointer $\text{Q}$.

  • Design $1: \text{Q}$ points to the node containing the front item.
     
  • Design $2: \text{Q}$ points to the node containing the rear item.

Which design is better?

  1. Design $1$ is better.
     
  2. Design $2$ is better.
     
  3. Both are the same.
     
  4. $\text{Q}$ should point to the middle node.
     
  5. A circular linked list cannot be used to represent a FIFO queue.

question.text:
Consider an array implementation of a queue. Suppose we try to keep all items at the front of a partially-filled array, so that $\texttt{data[0]}$ is always the front of the queue.

What would go wrong?

  1. The enqueue method would require linear time.
     
  2. The $\texttt{isEmpty}$ method would require linear time.
     
  3. The dequeue method would require linear time.
     
  4. None of the above.

question.text:
Consider an initially empty stack $\text{S}$ and an initially empty queue $\text{Q}$.

The following operations are performed:

S.push(5)
S.push(6)
S.push(S.top())
S.push(7)

Q.enqueue(S.pop())
Q.enqueue(5)
Q.enqueue(6)

print(Q.front())

S.push(Q.dequeue())

print(S.pop())

S.pop()

print(S.pop())

(Note : The front() function is used to access the first element stored in the queue.)

What will be printed?

  1. $567$
     
  2. $765$
     
  3. $775$
     
  4. None of the above
